ground_truth.description: The inspect.markcoroutinefunction(self) marking is unnecessary. AsyncMock awaits any side_effect return value for which asyncio.iscoroutine() is true, and __call__ is async def so it always returns a coroutine; the marker changes no behavior on any Python version (as the inline comment itself notes). It adds complexity without functional effect.

task.title: Enhance _uuid_dispatch with dispatch tracking and exception support
task.description:
Two related improvements to the `_uuid_dispatch` helper in `fused-memory/tests/test_rebuild_entity_summaries.py`:

1. **Dispatch tracking** — `_uuid_dispatch` currently doesn't verify that all mapped UUIDs were actually dispatched. If production code silently skips an entity, the mock won't catch it (tests rely on downstream aggregate assertions like `rebuilt == 2`). Add a tracking set inside `_side_effect` and expose an `assert_all_dispatched()` method or return the tracking set so callers can verify `len(called) == len(mapping)` after the test action.

2. **Exception support + unify _fail_uuid1** — `_fail_uuid1` (around line 826) duplicates the dispatch-by-uuid pattern but adds exception support. Extend `_uuid_dispatch` to accept mapping values that are either dicts (returned directly) or exceptions (raised), then rewrite `_fail_uuid1` as `_uuid_dispatch({'uuid-1': RuntimeError('FalkorDB timeout'), 'uuid-2': {...}})`. This eliminates duplication and enforces a single dispatch convention across the module.
